description: REGENERATED FROM THE AUTHORITATIVE M6 PHASE C WORK ORDER (not a verbatim recovery of the lost original). Common runtime owner + activation safety. Extract/reuse the existing OverlayService.LiveVideoRuntimePorts activation mechanic (pending/active/retiring, fresh per-ARM token, generation captured once after SceneRuntimeController.replaceRevision, invalidate-before-retire, matching(token), selectActiveRevision as the final ARM/promotion, abortActivation bounded cleanup) into a single principal common owner that can host STATIC Video AND Banner ports under one Android main owner thread. This is pure/JVM-testable owner-and-activation logic plus its unit tests; it does NOT add the Android clock/driver (FEAT-003), the Banner handler/restore/autostart (FEAT-004), or any provenance change (FEAT-005). Covers Phase C responsibilities: common runtime owner, promotion and eligibility (activation side), controller generation guarded delivery, one-installation / one-owner / Video-and-Banner-alternating invariants. Phase C scope items 1, 8 (activation portion), 9.
steps: Read docs/scenevibe-os-m6-banner-wall-clock-architecture.md sections 6, 7, 13, 22 and docs/m6-phase-a-architecture-report.md rows 4/5/6 first. Read OverlayService.LiveVideoRuntimePorts (lines ~390-585), VideoInstallationRuntimePorts.java, and SceneRuntimeController.java in full to understand the exact activation/generation/token semantics before touching anything.

Factor the common activation machinery (Activation{state/token/generation}, pending/active/retiring, nextActivation token minting with overflow fail-closed, invalidate(), matching(token), promotion via selection, abortActivation cleanup-retry) so a SINGLE principal owner can bind both a Video port set and a Banner port set as STATIC instances at the composition point. Do NOT introduce a second/competing LiveBanner owner and do NOT instantiate MediaSyncedTrackScheduler (the legacy scheduler stays a conserved definition, never reactivated). Preserve the exact existing Video behavior byte-for-behavior: existing M4PhaseF*/M5VideoCutover*/CloudReset* tests must still pass unchanged.

Introduce a Banner activation port surface (the WALL analogue of loadPreparedVideo/armPreparedManifest/selectActiveRevision) that: loads a prepared Banner calendar+manifest under PENDING only (pending NEVER renders); captures the SceneRuntimeController generation ONCE after replaceRevision; promotes PENDING->ACTIVE only after every prior ARM step succeeded; and routes DUE/EXIT to SceneRuntimeController.onEventDue/onEventExpired(id, capturedGeneration) using the active activation token only. Reuse SceneRuntimeController unchanged for presentation; it stays clock-free. The owner, not the controller, holds activation/token/generation.

Enforce the alternating-kind invariant in the owner: selecting Banner retires the Video visual owner(s) and clears/invalidates the MEDIA path before promotion; selecting Video invalidates the WALL activation/token (and later, in FEAT-003, cancels the WALL timer) before loading MEDIA. There is exactly one current installation, one principal owner, one active temporal path. No concurrent Video+Banner installation; no second renderer.

Initialize Banner local eligibility EXPLICITLY after promotion (the SceneRuntimeController.eligible flag survives loads per section 22), hide on suspension/overlay loss, and re-evaluate the current window on regain even if the eventId is identical. A pending-before-promotion callback is refused; only the active binding's callbacks are honored (stale token / stale generation = NO-OP).

Keep the owner Android-independent where the existing ports already are (BooleanSupplier owner predicate, Supplier<controller>, Runnable retire hooks, LongConsumer selection, Consumer<Boolean> diagnostics), so it is JVM-testable with fakes exactly like LiveVideoRuntimePorts is today. Any genuinely Android-only glue stays in OverlayService's composition, not in the testable owner core.

Add JVM tests (JUnit4, app/src/test/java/com/scenevibe/tvcompanionpoc/, following the M4PhaseFFixtures/M5VideoCutoverTest fake-ports style). Cover the section-13 race table for the Banner path and the shared owner: replacement just before DUE (old token invalidated, old DUE ignored); replacement during display (immediate retire then new package only); old EXPIRE after new ARM at the same eventId (token+generation prevent hiding the new scene); clear during wait (calendar emptied, runnable delivered as NO-OP); service stop/start (invalidation+retire at stop, fresh activation at start, no token reuse); pending callback before promotion (refused); Video<->Banner swap retires all visuals and neutralizes the other path; token/generation overflow fails ARM closed with no silent reuse. Prove exactly-one-visual-scene and pending-never-renders for Banner. Do NOT modify the pure wall/ scheduler and do NOT touch MediaCalendarScheduler.
acceptance_criteria: A single principal common owner hosts static Video and Banner activation ports; no competing LiveBanner owner exists and MediaSyncedTrackScheduler is not instantiated.
Banner callbacks route to SceneRuntimeController.onEventDue/onEventExpired(id, capturedGeneration) under the active token only; pending never renders; stale token/generation callbacks are NO-OPs.

Promotion happens only after all prior ARM steps succeed; Banner local eligibility is initialized after promotion and re-evaluated on regain; Video<->Banner selection retires the opposite visual owner and neutralizes the opposite temporal path (one installation / one owner / alternating kinds).
Existing Video owner behavior is preserved: all pre-existing OverlayService/owner-related JVM tests still pass unchanged; MediaCalendarScheduler and the pure wall/ scheduler are byte-unchanged.

New JVM tests cover the section-13 race table for the Banner/common-owner path and pass under :app:testDebugUnitTest (or, if no Android SDK, compile and pass under the project's JVM test task when provisioned); token/generation overflow fails ARM closed.
verification: cd tests && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s . -p "test_*.py" (still 141 OK; pure WALL contract still 68/68; owner changes must not touch the pure wall/ package or the 287 inventory yet)
git diff --check; confirm app/src/main/java/.../wall/*.java and app/src/main/java/.../calendar/MediaCalendarScheduler.java are byte-unchanged (git diff --stat)

If an Android SDK can be provisioned under OPEN_INTERNET: Gradle :app:testDebugUnitTest --console=plain (new owner tests + all existing tests pass). Otherwise declare the Android unit figure as a CI-only gate honestly and rely on code review + the host Python/JDK gate.
findings: IMPLEMENTED (FEAT-002, regenerated from the authoritative Phase C work order, not a verbatim recovery). Added four new UNTRACKED files, no existing tracked file modified at all (git diff --stat empty), so the frozen pure wall/*.java and calendar/MediaCalendarScheduler.java are byte-unchanged by construction. Files: (1) app/src/main/java/com/scenevibe/tvcompanionpoc/BannerPreparedState.java - memory-only trusted Banner parse state (pure wall WallCalendar + already-validated OverlayManifest with product=banner/clockMode=wall/pauseBehavior=continue) plus a static arm(state,ports,revision) orchestrator that mirrors VideoPreparedState.arm's ordered retire->load->armManifest->select discipline and aborts to ARM_FAILED on any partial failure. (2) BannerInstallationRuntimePorts.java - the WALL analogue of VideoInstallationRuntimePorts (isOwnerThread/retireVideoVisualOwner/retireManifestedVisualOwner/loadPreparedBanner/armPreparedManifest/selectActiveBanner/onWallResult/abortActivation). (3) LiveBannerRuntimePorts.java - the testable common-owner Banner activation core, a direct REUSE of OverlayService.LiveVideoRuntimePorts' mechanic: pending/active/retiring Activation records; a fresh unique token minted per ARM even same-revision ('banner-activation-'+(++nextActivation)) with Long.MAX_VALUE overflow failing ARM closed (no silent reuse); SceneRuntimeController generation captured ONCE after replaceRevision (negative generation refused); invalidate()-before-retire; matching(token) honoring only the active binding; selectActiveBanner as the final ARM/promotion step; onWallResult routing an already-selected pure WallCalendarScheduler.Result (EXIT then DUE) to the reused SceneRuntimeController.onEventExpired/onEventDue(id, capturedGeneration) under the active token only; alternating-kind retireVideoVisualOwner()+neutralizeMedia() before promotion; Banner local eligibility initialized explicitly AFTER promotion (controller eligible flag survives loads per section 22) via diagnostics.accept(true)+controller.onEligibility(true); onEligibility(token,false) hides immediately, regain re-evaluates the current window on the next result even for an identical eventId; abortActivation bounded idempotent cleanup. Kept Android-independent exactly like the Video ports (BooleanSupplier owner, Supplier<SceneRuntimeController>, Runnable retire/neutralize hooks, LongConsumer selection, Consumer<Boolean> diagnostics). NO second/competing LiveBanner authority; MediaSyncedTrackScheduler is never instantiated or referenced; SceneRuntimeController reused UNCHANGED; the Android WALL clock/driver/timer is deliberately NOT added (deferred to FEAT-003) and nothing was added to the pure wall/ package. DEFERRED / NOT DONE (by scope): the InstallationHandler/registry/codec wiring, OverlayService composition that binds these Banner ports as a STATIC instance under the real main-thread owner, the Android WALL clock/driver/timer, restore, Banner-aware autostart, diagnostics taxonomy, and the provenance baseline extension are FEAT-003/004/005. No PR/push performed (orchestrator owns that). REVIEW-FIX (iteration 1, 2026-10-07-090148-review.md NEEDS_CHANGES): fixed the confirmed owner<->driver promotion-seam bug. In LiveBannerRuntimePorts.selectActiveBanner the active binding is now established (active=pending; pending=null) BEFORE invoking the selection sink, instead of after. The real OverlayService composition arms the WALL driver INSIDE the Banner selection sink (revision -> { activeRevision = revision; armWallDriver(); }), and WallClockDriver.arm synchronously loads the pure calendar at a fresh epoch and emits the first result back through owner.onWallResult. Previously that first emit landed while active==null, so matching(token) returned null and the first DUE was dropped; the <=1s heartbeat uses the idempotent scheduler.evaluate (not load) so a window already live at promotion never re-emitted until a SCREEN_ON/resume forced a load-based reselect. Setting active before the sink makes matching(token) honor the active binding when the synchronous first emit lands, so a window live at promotion renders exactly one scene immediately after promotion. The pending-never-renders invariant is preserved: no callback is honored before the active assignment, and promotion has fully succeeded (every prior ARM-step guard passed) by that point; a future-start window still shows nothing until a later fresh fire.
